prompt: Design a fitness training app for runners — track workouts, streaks, and personal records. It needs a home dashboard with today's workout and metrics, a workout library to browse and start guided runs, and a profile screen with goals and settings. Make it feel athletic, motivating, and modern.
title: Run Training

issues.description: The verified screen file is being built from a generic dashboard composition, and the displayed imports/config suggest non-running UI patterns rather than a purpose-built 'Today's run' home. The brief requires a scoreboard-style workout-first landing with start CTA, streak status, and four concrete fitness metrics.

The library screen should help runners browse guided workouts by distance, duration, and intensity with a quick-start path. The current composition appears to be a broad list-detail scaffold rather than a focused running workout browser with concise workout cards and the required search/filter pattern.

Workout detail must clearly explain one guided run, including distance, time expectations, intensity, and coach notes, with a prominent start control. The verified file structure indicates generic screen scaffolding, so the required workout-specific detail experience is not evident.

Progress overview must summarize personal records, weekly totals, and recent workout history. The current verified screen composition is not clearly aligned to those outcomes and appears to inherit generic dashboard patterns instead of a compact running performance view.

Profile settings needs a focused training preferences screen with editable goals, units, notifications, and account preferences. The verified screen appears to be assembled from generic app dashboard patterns and does not clearly show the required running-specific settings structure.

Button uses token names like bg-primary, text-primary-foreground, focus-visible:ring-ring, and ring-offset-background. If these are not mapped to the brief's required CSS variables, the component will drift from token discipline; it should be explicitly aligned to the provided custom properties.

Badge variants reference success-subtle and warning-subtle, which are not part of the provided token list. This risks inconsistent rendering and weaker contrast unless remapped to the sanctioned tokens.
Cards use shadow-sm by default, which is softer than the brief's restrained hairline-border surfaces. Reduce emphasis on shadows so the athletic high-contrast language stays crisp and minimal.

The screen includes a social/activity log section with runner names and mixed status text that feels like a feed, not a personal today dashboard. It lacks a strong single dominant workout moment and a clear streak/PR hierarchy.
Large vertical gaps and multiple separated panels make the page feel sparse and unfocused. The scoreboard, chart, and log all compete without a clear primary action focus.
'Recent run log rows: Easy 5K, Intervals 8x400, Long run 12K...' reads like a developer note rather than product copy.
The screen appears duplicated with multiple overlapping profile/edit sections and repeated bottom nav, creating a broken, crowded composition.
Settings are not compact or coherent: several toggles are shouted in all caps and the screen mixes profile summary, goal cards, and duplicate action areas without a clean settings model.
Repeated 'Save changes' and 'Cancel' controls across separate panes feel inconsistent and make the interface look unfinished.
Key stats are mislabeled or unit-incoherent: 'Best 5K' shows 18.2 km, 'Longest run' shows 3:02 km, and 'Total runs' shows 1,759 count. These are not believable personal records.
The progress chart header says 'Weekly distance' while the right-side unit label says 'kcal', which conflicts with the chart data and undermines trust.
The toolbar mixes search, filter, and action in a way that feels crowded and uneven; the chart and table compete without a clear dominant focus.
The hero area is fine, but the main workout section is filled with four identical zero-state cards that read as placeholders rather than step-by-step guided guidance.
All capture tiles show 0.0 km, 0 min, 0 pace, 0 kcal, which looks like uninitialized data and does not fulfill guided workout playback.
The repeated empty cards create an unfinished feel and violate the one dominant moment rule by making the screen look like a template.
The card grid is dominated by oversized blank cards with centered placeholder icons instead of image-first run cards. This feels empty and not premium or athletic.
Workout cards do not show enough specific guidance up front. The screen should emphasize run name, distance/time, and coaching goal more clearly in each card.
Toolbar labels and actions feel generic ('Search', 'Back') and the page lacks the direct, punchy coaching language expected from the Nike direction.

reviewResult.summary: The build is not ready for approval because the verified screens do not clearly demonstrate the required running-app experiences for today, library, workout detail, progress, and profile, and several shared components are not yet clearly disciplined to the provided token system. The product should be tightened around specific fitness metrics, guided workouts, and direct coaching copy.
requiredFixes: src/screens/home-dashboard.jsx: Replace the generic app-dashboard composition with a true today dashboard for running: today's workout, 9-day streak, four scoreboard metrics (weekly distance, avg pace, streak, calories), and one dominant Start run CTA. Remove non-fitness navigation/content patterns and ensure the copy matches the brief's direct coaching voice.

src/screens/workout-library.jsx: Present the guided workout library as a browse-and-pick experience with workout cards or a compact table showing workout name, distance/time, focus, status, and last done. The screen should include search + select filter + primary action, and the content must stay within running workouts only.

src/screens/workout-detail.jsx: Make the workout detail screen explain the selected guided run with total distance, estimated time, intensity, coach notes, and a clear Start now control. If you show guided playback prep, keep capture limited to distance, time, and calories and avoid unrelated dashboard chrome.

src/screens/progress-overview.jsx: Rebuild the progress overview around personal records, weekly totals, and recent workout history, with the required metric set (Best 5K, Longest run, Best week, Total runs) and a weekly distance chart. Ensure all rows and labels are run-domain specific and comparison-based.

src/screens/profile-settings.jsx: Replace any generic settings or unrelated screen chrome with a focused running profile page covering training goals, weekly/monthly targets, units, voice coaching, reminders, and streak alerts. Use compact editable rows/selects and keep copy concise and concrete.

src/components/Button.jsx: Add an explicit focus-visible style that maps to the theme token system used by the app and verify all button variants respect the high-contrast athletic palette. The current component relies on shadcn-style token names that may not match the brief's token discipline unless wired correctly in the theme.

src/components/Badge.jsx: Align badge variants to the provided design tokens and ensure success/warning/muted states remain legible on the dark athletic system. Avoid relying on undefined subtle token names unless they are guaranteed by the theme.

src/components/Card.jsx: Adjust card styling to match the brief's minimal hairline-border look without unnecessary shadow emphasis on static panels. The design language calls for restrained surfaces and stronger contrast, not soft generic cards.

home-dashboard: Replace the unrelated news-feed style list with a true running-focused dashboard. Keep one dominant hero moment, and convert the lower section into streak/PR modules and a clear workout start CTA instead of generic activity rows.

profile-settings: Remove the duplicated profile panes and conflicting buttons. Consolidate into one profile screen with editable training goals, units, notifications, and account preferences; make the primary Save action singular and prominent.

progress-overview: Fix metric copy and units so every stat is domain-correct and concrete. 'Best 5K' should not show km as the value unit, 'Total runs' should not be labeled count with an enormous nonsensical number, and the chart axis/title labels must match the data.

workout-detail: Replace the empty placeholder icon cards with a guided workout playback layout. Show interval steps, distance/time/calorie capture, and clear coaching prompts; avoid repeated zero-state metrics across four identical cards.

workout-library: The library grid is too empty and generic. Replace placeholder icon cards with real guided run cards that show workout name, distance or duration, and coaching goal, and make the toolbar simpler with one search, one select filter, and one primary action.
